title: Al-Haqqah as a whole: meaning and tadabbur: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Al-Haqqah; noon and meem recap and when letters meet
source: Written for quran/y8 lesson 22 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Al-Haqqah as a whole rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 22. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

timeline.text: The Inevitable Reality: the Day is certain
Nations who denied it: Thamud, 'Aad, Fir'awn, Nuh's people
The Day: the Trumpet, the two records
The Qur'an is truth from the Lord of the worlds

panels.title: Lessons
points: Denial of the truth has consequences
Our record is being written now
Feed the poor, believe in Allah

panels.title: Structure helps hifdh
points: Know which part you are in
Themes stop jumps between similar ayat

keywords.def: reflecting deeply on the meaning of the Qur'an
revision of what is already memorised

questions.q: In the portal response box, write a four-sentence summary of Al-Haqqah, one sentence per part (sentence starter: 'Al-Haqqah begins by ...').
questions.a: Four accurate sentences matching the four parts.

questions.q: Complete the summary in the portal box, then recite the first three ayat of each part to a partner. Today's rota group recites Al-Haqqah to the teacher.
questions.a: Summary complete; partner ticks each part.

questions.q: Extend: choose one ayah that affects you most and explain why.
questions.a: Personal response linked to a correct ayah.

questions.q: Stretch: find two other surahs that also describe the two records (right and left hand).
questions.a: Al-Inshiqaq (84:7 to 12) and Al-Waqi'ah or Al-Isra'; at least Al-Inshiqaq.
A) the truth of the Qur'an. The final part defends the Qur'an as revelation and ends with tasbih.

questions.q: Think again: If you had to explain Al-Haqqah to a friend in four sentences, what would they be?
questions.a: The Day is certain (1 to 3); nations who denied it were destroyed (4 to 12); the Day and the two records (13 to 37); the Qur'an is truth from Allah (38 to 52).
